recentItems.title: eThekwini's update on last council meeting
recentItems.description:
eThekwini Mayor Cyril Xaba held a post-Council media briefing in Durban, following the last Council meeting of the term. 

He provides updates on the city's water situation, service delivery challenges, and key Council decisions aimed at stimulating economic growth and attracting investment. 

SABC News reporter Mlondi Radebe is there with more.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: EQUESTRIAN | 2026 Toyota SA Derby to showcase the best  talent in the country
recentItems.description:
The 2026 Toyota SA Derby has been taking place from October 1 to 4, 2026, at the Kyalami Equestrian Park in Midrand, marking the 61st edition of South Africa's premier and most demanding showjumping event.

Served as the grand finale of the Ultimate 4x4 Series, this event featured the traditional 1,200-meter course with 18 challenging obstacles designed by Kate Launder and Milton Kgole. 

Thando Mxoli is in Kyalami to give us some more information about this event. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: GBVF hotline has seen about 300 calls per day - Dina Pule.  #sabcnews
recentItems.description:
Minister for Social Development, Dina Pule says the number of calls the department's hotline is receiving has increased since the incidents of the killing of women at Ekurhuleni in Gauteng. At least twelve women have died in Gauteng over the past three months. Pule was speaking in Cape Town during a media engagement session to outline the work of the department on Gender Based Violence among others. Pule who also co-chair the Presidential Inter-Ministerial Committee on GBV says on avarage the department is receiving about three hundred calls per day, but that has since changed signaling panic and concern among the citizens.

Credit: Mlamli Maneli

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Jukulyn residents feel safer but there are still challenges
recentItems.description:
Jukuly residents say their area is much safer since the introduction of new security companies. This as the country put a spotlight on gender-based violence.

President Cyril Ramphosa this week announced four immediate measures to deal with GBVF. One of which is for every municipality to conduct a women's safety audit. 

The audits must identify broken streetlights, overgrown grass in public spaces, abandoned buildings, unsafe transport routes and facilities, poorly secured parks and other conditions that place women at risk. 

SABC News Reporter Ofentse Setimo is visiting one of the affected communities.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Thembisa murder victim Boitumelo Mashita laid to rest
recentItems.description:
The funeral of 23-year-old Boitumelo Mashita, who was shot and killed allegedly by her estranged husband while on her way to work last Monday, is underway at her home in Thembisa in Ekurhuleni. 

She was the 12th woman to be murdered in Ekurhuleni since July this year. Her estranged husband, who was the person of interest in her murder, was later found dead in Midrand. 

SABC News reporter Refilwe Mekoa is at the funeral.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Ekurhuleni murders | A final farewell for Nomfesane Mjobo
recentItems.description:
The family of Nomfesane Mjobo is preparing to lay her to rest in her hometown of Lusikisiki. Mjobo is among the 12 women whose bodies were discovered in Ekurhuleni, with her remains repatriated to the Eastern Cape on Friday. 

Her burial comes as questions continue to mount over the circumstances surrounding the deaths, with growing calls for safer communities. 

We cross live now to SABC News Reporter Fundiswa Mhlekude, who is there with the latest.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | New political party 'Born To Win' sets its eyes on Polokwane Municipality
recentItems.description:
A new political party, Born To Win, is expected to contest in the Polokwane Municipality.

The party is led by Boy Mamabolo - a former ANC MP who left the party after being left out as an MP in the previous elections.

The party is expected to address service delivery challenges and unresolved matters in the area.

For more, let's cross to our reporter Katlego Nyoni in Polokwane.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | SACP launches Red October campaign in Eastern Cape
recentItems.description:
SACP General Secretary, Solly Mapaila, is launching the party's Red October campaign in Komga. 

The campaign is aimed at mobilising workers and poor communities around economic and political issues. 

This year's Red October campaign is launched just month before the Local Government Elections of which the SACP will be contesting for the first time.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | BOSA on a campaign trail in Mangaung
recentItems.description:
Build One South Africa (BOSA) leader Mmusi Maimane is taking the party's 2026 local government election manifesto to Mangaung in the Free State. 

Mangaung is one of 24 municipalities BOSA is contesting in its first local government election. 

SABC News Reporter Kamogelo Seekoei joins us for more.

recentItems.title: 26-year-old innovator develops Maths app to help learners prepare for exams
recentItems.description:
The finish line is in sight for matric learners, but there's still work to be done. As they enter the final stretch of exam preparation, a young developer is hoping technology can help make the journey a little easier, particularly when it comes to Mathematics.

To hear more about the app and how it could help matric learners prepare for their exams, we're joined in the studio by its young developer, Lesedi Mochadibane.
